rules.title: Rent Stabilization Ordinance (RSO) allowable annual rent increase
rules.requirement: Rent on RSO units may be increased once every 12 months by the allowable rent increase percentage. Effective February 2, 2026, the landlord can no longer include an additional percentage increase for utilities. Rent may be reset to market rate when the tenant voluntarily moves out, accepts a Tenant Buyout Agreement, or is evicted for certain listed reasons.
rules.key_value: Once every 12 months by the allowable rent increase percentage
rules.coverage_text: Rental properties in the City of Los Angeles first built on or before October 1, 1978, plus replacement units under LAMC Section 151.28, including apartments, condominiums, townhomes, duplexes, two or more single-family dwelling units on the same parcel, hotel/motel/rooming house rooms occupied by the same tenant for more than 30 consecutive days, residential units attached to a commercial building, ADUs, JADUs, and mobile homes and recreational vehicles in mobile home parks.
rules.exemptions: For condominiums and townhomes, the rent amount is not regulated for tenancies that commenced after December 31, 1995. A landlord can apply for a luxury exemption from the RSO if they can establish the monthly rent charged on or before May 31, 1978.
rules.quoted_span: Rent may be increased once every 12 months by the allowable rent increase percentage

rules.title: RSO additional tenant rent increase
rules.requirement: Effective February 2, 2026, an additional 10% increase for an additional dependent added to the tenancy is no longer permitted. A 10% increase is allowed for an additional tenant (not a dependent) who moves into the unit, and the landlord can increase the rent within 60 days of learning about the additional tenant.

rules.title: RSO legal reasons for eviction
rules.requirement: Tenancies in RSO units may be ended only for listed reasons. At-fault reasons are failure to pay rent, failure to fix a lease violation, nuisance or damage, illegal use, failure to renew a similar rental agreement, failure to provide reasonable access, or an unapproved subtenant at lease end. No-fault reasons are owner or immediate family move-in, resident manager move-in, demolition and permanent removal from the rental market, government order, or conversion to affordable housing.

rules.title: RSO relocation assistance and notice for no-fault evictions
rules.requirement: No-fault evictions of RSO tenants require payment of tenant relocation assistance. The landlord must file a Landlord Declaration of Intent to Evict with LAHD and give the tenant a 30-day and 60-day written notice (some evictions require 120-day notice or up to a 1-year extension).

rules.title: Filing of termination notices with LAHD
rules.requirement: All notices to terminate a tenancy for RSO rental units must be filed with the Los Angeles Housing Department within three (3) business days of service on the tenant.
